lessons.title: Triton kernel: dynamic-bound loops must not use Python range()
lessons.symptom: Review flagged vllm_ascend/ops/triton/mamba/postprocess.py: `for i in range(0, copy_size, COPY_BLOCK_SIZE)` where copy_size is a runtime value — Triton evaluates range() at compile time and requires constexpr bounds, so compilation fails (or silently miscompiles) once the copy path runs.
lessons.root_cause: The Triton kernel copy loop was written with Python range() semantics; Triton only allows compile-time-constant bounds there.  Runtime bounds need a `while` loop (Triton 2.x+) or tl.static_range with a constexpr cap + runtime mask.
fix_guidance: In any Triton kernel, check every loop bound: if it is loaded from a pointer, derived from runtime tensors, or passed as a non-constexpr arg, it is NOT valid for range()
Use `while i < copy_size:` with `i += BLOCK` or `tl.static_range(MAX_ITERS)` + `if i < num_iters:` mask
After syncing a kernel from upstream, grep for `range(` with non-constexpr bounds before merging
lessons.example: gemini code review on PR #13823 flagged mamba/postprocess.py:166; the upstream vllm kernel this was synced from uses the same loop shape, so verify against upstream's while-loop pattern.
